title: Chat event
description: One event in a chat session, by its `kind`: the person's message, the agent's words, a tool the agent is using, an approval asked or settled, or a system line. The host stamps `at`, `session` and `seq`. A tool's raw input and output are never part of an event.
$comment: The chat package's own contract (D-036, D-037; api.md 98-101). Kinds follow nclite's EVENT_KINDS (engine/store/log.ts) plus tool_activity; approval facts follow nclite's container/approval-ask.ts. Versioned in the $id path like the ledger's.

sessionId.description: A chat session id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 64, not starting with a hyphen (a UUID fits).

approvalId.description: An approval id, as the approval request gave it: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 64.

seq.description: The event's place in its session, from 1. A client that reconnects passes the last one it saw.

text.description: Words, not blank, up to 100,000 characters.

path.description: A file or folder path, up to 4096 characters, with no control, line-break or text-direction character.
path.$comment: As nclite's LINE_BREAKING (engine/approvals/facts.ts): the path is the subject of the question the person reads.

fileLabel.description: The name the person's file has, to show them: display only, never in the agent's prompt, and nothing is believed from it. Up to 200 characters, with no control, line-break or text-direction character.
fileLabel.$comment: D-068, point 356: a wholly non-Latin name saves as `file.png`, and the person should still see their own name.

agent.description: Which command-line agent runs the session: `claude` (Claude Code) or `kiro` (Kiro CLI).

model.description: The model the agent uses, as the agent's own command line names it (such as `opus`); left out for the agent's default.

stamp.description: What every event carries: when, which session, and its place in the session.

chip.description: Something the person attached to a message: one of their notes or one card.

ref.description: The note's `seq`, or the card's number.

label.description: What the chip shows: the card's title, or the start of the note.

attachedFile.description: A file the person attached to a message, saved under the board's folder; the agent opens it by its path.

name.description: The file's name as saved: letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, up to 80 characters, no leading dot.

path.description: Where it is, relative to the board's folder: `.visionboard/attachments/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<n>-<name>`.

size.description: Its size in bytes, at most 10 MB.

label.description: The name the person's file has, to show them; left out when it was not given. Display only.

chips.description: The notes and cards sent with it; left out when none.

files.description: The files attached to it; left out when none. At most 10 a message as sent; messages joined while the agent works carry them all.

messageOut.description: The agent's words: a finished block of text partway through its turn (`interim`), or the reply it ended on.

interim.description: Present, and true, only for words said partway through the turn; absent means the reply the turn ended on.

toolActivity.description: A tool the agent is using, by its short name and state. For a board write it also names the board, the cards and the ledger position, so the page can show what changed. Never the tool's raw input or output.

call.description: The agent's id for this tool call, so its `running` and its end pair up.

tool.description: The tool's short name, such as `Read`, `Bash` or `write_board`.

board.description: For a board write: the board it wrote on.

cards.description: For a board write that is done: the numbers of the cards it drew or changed.

head.description: For a board write that is done: the ledger position after it.

approvalRequest.description: The agent is waiting to read or change a file or run a command until the person allows or denies it; silence past `expiresAt` is a denial, and with no `expiresAt` the question waits for the person with no limit (approvalHold).

approvalId.description: The approval's id; the person's answer names it.

expiresAt.description: When the request lapses, denied; absent, it waits until the person answers, presses Stop or sends a new message.

scopes.description: The scopes a yes may have, `once` always: `session` unless the call can't be remembered, `folder` only inside the board's folder. Absent: `once` and `session` (an older host).

approvalResult.description: How an approval was settled: allowed, denied, lapsed, or released by a Stop or a new message.

approved.description: True only when the person allowed it.

system.description: A line from the host, not the agent: a session started or resumed, a turn ended, stopped or failed.

turn.description: Present when this line ends the agent's turn: `done`, `stopped` (the person pressed Stop) or `error`.

writeFacts.description: A file the agent is about to create or change.

op.description: `create` a new file, `replace` one whole, `edit` part of one, or `append` to one.

preview.description: A short preview of the change, for the person to read; left out when there is nothing to show.

commandFacts.description: A shell command the agent is about to run.

command.description: The command, exactly as it would run.

risks.description: The names of the risky patterns the command matched; empty when none was recognised.

paths.description: The files and folders the command names; empty when none was recognised.

readFacts.description: A file the agent is about to read, or with `recursive` every file under a folder (a search).

recursive.description: Present when every file under the folder is read, as a search does.

facts.description: What the agent is about to do, as facts, never a sentence: a file read or write, or a shell command.

status.description: `approved` or `denied` by the person (or by an answer kept for the session), `expired` (nobody answered in time) or `released` (a Stop or a new message ended the wait).

scope.description: How long a yes holds: `once`, for the rest of the `session`, or for this `folder` (remembered across sessions; inside the board's folder only). A remembered yes covers writes under that file's folder, or that command's first words, never a refused path.

settled.description: `approved` is true exactly when `status` is `approved`, and only a yes has a `scope`.

answer.description: The person's answer to an approval request.

approved.description: True to allow it, false to deny it. Required: there is no default.

scope.description: How long a yes holds: `once` (the default), the rest of the `session`, or this `folder`.

outcome.description: What the gate is told: go on only when `approved` is true.

approved.description: True to go on; anything else is a refusal the agent is told.

approvalId.description: The approval the person was asked; left out when nobody was asked.

asked.description: Present, and false, only when nobody was asked: the access rules decided (allowed, or denied whatever the answer), or a yes kept for the session or the folder.
